title: Chapter 81: Core of the Truehearted 3
content:
Chapter 81

Core of the Truehearted 3

Wei Wuxian folded the two sheets of paper and slid them back into his inner lapel with smooth theatricality, eyes wide in mock shock. "Well, well, color me surprised. Still got plenty of spiritual juice in the tank, don’t you? Congratulations! But tell me, if you weren't scheming something foul, why hide the fact that your golden core is firing on all cylinders?"

Of course, those pages weren't pages ripped from the Collection of Turmoil inside Jin Guangyao’s private vault. They were the transcriptions Lan Wangji had inked from memory down in the forbidden archives. Lan Wangji had handed one copy to Lan Xichen, and Wei Wuxian had pocketed the remaining two. Pulling them out just now was pure bait, engineered to make Su She sweat. Layer that on top of Wei Wuxian’s relentless taunts, and Su She had snapped. Without needing a single cue, Lan Wangji had lunged with a test strike, and Su She had taken the bait hook, line, and sinker.

The crowd scrambled out of the splash zone. Not that they needed to—when Lan Wangji threw down, he was every bit as suffocating and relentless as Wei Wuxian’s sharp tongue. He left zero breathing room, forcing Su She to burn through every ounce of spiritual power just to keep his head attached. Stumbling back onto the stairs, Su She glanced down. Right beneath his boots was the crimson warding array.

Lan Wangji’s jaw set into stone.

Bad move, Wei Wuxian thought, his stomach dropping. He’s going to trash the ward!

Sure enough, Su She bit straight through his tongue, pooling a mouthful of blood and spraying it across the floor. A thick, crimson splatter masked the faint lines of the array. Abandoning the duel, Lan Wangji dragged the edge of Bichen across his own left palm, dropping low to frantically redraw the broken runes. Seizing the distraction, Su She whipped a talisman from his robes and slammed it down. A brilliant plume of azure flame and choking smoke erupted across the stones.

A teleportation talisman!

Back at the Chang Clan cemetery in Yueyang, the masked grave robber had moved with the distinct, razor-sharp forms of Gusu Lan swordsmanship. As an outside disciple originally trained by the Lans, Su Minshan checked every single box.

The mysterious face-obscured phantom haunting their steps was Su She all along!

Wei Wuxian dropped down beside Lan Wangji. "How bad is it?"

Lan Wangji traced his bloodied fingers over the rock, then gave a slow, grim shake of his head. Fresh blood had completely corrupted the original array; it was beyond patching. Reaching down, Wei Wuxian gently took his hand, using his own dark sleeve to wipe away the grime and gore. "Leave it, then. Don't waste your breath."

The array was on its last legs, shuddering like glass under a hammer. The Moling Su disciples looked utterly lost. Clearly, Su She hadn't bothered to let his own boys in on the joke; he hadn't told them they were playing a cursed tune, nor had he taught them how to shield their own cores. In his grand master plan, these loyal followers were meant to be slaughtered alongside everyone else. Terrified of the boiling resentment in the room, the disciples huddled together in a trembling knot.

Yet nobody in the cavern had the bandwidth to settle scores. Panic tore through the ranks. Clan leaders grabbed their sons by the shoulders, screaming over the din: "The second they breach, don't look back! Protect yourself and run! Just stay alive, do you hear me?!"

Jin Ling listened, his chest tightening with a sour ache. Part of him secretly hoped his own uncle would say something—anything—like that. He waited and waited, but Jiang Cheng didn't make a sound. Unable to help himself, Jin Ling burned a hole into the side of Jiang Cheng's face with a desperate, heavy stare.

He stared so hard that Jiang Cheng finally turned around. The dark scowl on his brow softened for a fraction of a second, only to twist into irritation. "What's wrong with your eyes?"

Jin Ling huffed, crossing his arms. "Nothing!"

Wei Wuxian tore a clean strip of fabric from his inner cuff, carefully wrapping the cut on Lan Wangji’s palm. Suddenly, a figure lunged from behind, swinging a sword straight for his skull! Lan Wangji’s right hand whipped out; with a crisp, metallic chime, his bare fingers flicked the incoming steel away like a fly.

Wei Wuxian turned to look. "Seriously? You again?"

The sheer force of Lan Wangji’s flick sent the attacker sprawling across the dirt. It was Yi Weichun. Eyes bloodshot, he clutched his blade, wheezing, "Wei Wuxian! I don't believe a single goddamn word out of your mouth!"

Wei Wuxian sighed. "The game is up, and Su She literally used his spiritual power to cut and run. What else is there left to deny?"

Yi Weichun swung wildly from the floor, bellowing, "I don't care! If it comes out of your mouth, it's a lie!"

Hatred had blinded him completely; a man consumed by a grudge would rather swallow poison than admit his mortal enemy might be in the right.

Right on cue, shrieks of pure, unadulterated terror echoed from the entrance:

"It's broken!"

"The barrier shattered!"

"They're inside!"

Wen Ning hurled a cluster of tattered corpses through the air with his bare hands, but he was still just one man holding the line. Stripped of its blood ward, the Demon-Subduing Cave was entirely defenseless against the churning black tide of the undead. The suffocating reek of rot and a chorus of feral roars flooded the cavern in an instant.

Jin Ling had never faced this many walking corpses at point-blank range. The hair on his neck stood on end as his knuckles went white around Suihua’s hilt. Suddenly, his fingers were pried open, and a freezing piece of silver was shoved into his palm. Looking down, he stammered, "Jiujiu...?"

Jiang Cheng stood swaying, leaning heavily on Sandu’s lifeless steel. "If you dare lose Zidian, I'll break your legs!"

Lan Sizhui and Lan Jingyi drew their swords, lunging toward the breach. "Ghost General! We've got your back!"

Sect Leader Ouyang, unable to stand, clawed frantically at his son’s robes, roaring, "Zizhen, get back here!"

Ouyang Zizhen hacked at an incoming corpse, shouting over his shoulder, "Don't be scared, Dad! I'll protect you!"

That split second of divided attention was nearly fatal—a withered, blackened claw lunged straight for his throat! Sect Leader Ouyang’s soul practically left his body as he shrieked, "Zizhen!"

A streak of steel severed the rotting limb in the nick of time. Lan Qiren grabbed Ouyang Zizhen by the collar, chucked him back into the safety of the crowd, and spearheaded a vanguard of Lan swordsmen directly into the fray. Having rested for a good while, his stamina was mostly restored; his blade moved with such razor-sharp precision that the surrounding cultivators stared in dumbfounded awe.

Lan Sizhui’s sword whipped through the air like a gale. A loud clang rang behind him as an incoming ambush was deflected off his blind spot. Sizhui turned, astonished. "Young Master Jin?! What are you doing out here?!"

Seeing everyone his age throwing down, Jin Ling hadn't been able to sit on his hands. The second Jiang Cheng looked away, he’d shoved Zidian back into his uncle’s palm and sprinted headfirst into the kill zone. Jiang Cheng tried to pursue, stumbling through a few clumsy swings, Sandu feeling heavy as a mountain in his drained grip. Two female corpses lunged from his flanks. Cursing, he raised his blade—only for a pair of pale hands to rip the ghouls to shreds.

"Sect Leader Ji—"

Hearing that voice made Jiang Cheng’s vision go red. He kicked Wen Ning away with all his might, snarling, "Get the fuck away from me!" Then he roared across the cavern, "Jin Ling!"

Lan Jingyi shuddered. "You'd better get back! Your uncle is about to sprout fangs and eat you alive."

Jin Ling ignored the roar, which sounded far more terrifying than the corpses in front of him. "You go back!"

Ouyang Zizhen broke free from his father’s grip and charged right back to the frontlines. "Whoa, I had no clue Old Master Lan was this cracked with a blade! His swordplay is insane!"

Lan Jingyi yelled back proudly, "Duh! Who do you think taught Hanguang-jun and Ze-wu-jun how to hold a sword before they were sixteen?!"

Gritting his teeth, Sect Leader Ouyang joined the fray, bellowing at the paralyzed cultivators in the back: "What are you all waiting for?! It's kill or be killed! Even the kids are bleeding out here—get off your useless asses!"

Shamed by the sheer grit of the younger generation, more and more cultivators drew their blades, burning whatever scraps of physical stamina they had left. Slowly but surely, the suffocating swarm pressing at the mouth of the cave began to thin. Half an hour later, the relentless tide had dwindled to scattered stragglers.

Against all odds, the tide was turning!

When Lan Wangji cleaved the final charging corpse clean in half, the Demon-Subduing Cave was a slaughterhouse. Bodies lay in heaps, and rivers of black blood pooled across the stone.

Every single person was caked in dried, crusty gore, their lungs burning with the nauseating stench of iron and rot. With the adrenaline draining away, cultivators collapsed like puppets with cut strings, sprawling across the floorboards indistinguishable from corpses. Only a handful of clan leaders and the resilient youths remained on their feet, propped up by their swords.

Lan Jingyi’s eyes were glassy, his face white as paper. "I... I've never killed that many in my life... I took down at least thirty... no, forty on my own..."

Ouyang Zizhen wheezed, "S-Same... here..."

As if on cue, the boys dropped like stones, planting their faces straight into the dirt, utterly spent.

Jiang Cheng dragged his leaden boots over to Jin Ling, hauling the boy upright by his collar. "Are you hurt?!"

Jin Ling’s breath came in ragged, metallic gasps. "No, I'm—"

Smack!

Jiang Cheng cuffed him across the back of the head, knocking him back to the ground. "Not hurt?! Then take a beating so you learn your damn lesson! You think my words are a joke, you little brat?!"

Yet the swing drained the last of his strength; Jiang Cheng collapsed onto the floor beside him, chest heaving as his eyes drifted toward the two figures standing guard at the cavern’s threshold.

Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji were a total mess. Dressed in black, Wei Wuxian didn't look too bad, but Lan Wangji’s pristine white robes were painted in a horrifying mosaic of black and crimson gore. The only thing on his person that remained immaculate was that sacred forehead ribbon. In his grip, Bichen still hummed with steady, effortless spiritual flow.

Nobody had ever seen Hanguang-jun looking this disheveled, but right now, everyone was too battered to care.

A weak voice croaked from the back: "Is it... over...?"

Hearing that voice, the room shared a collective shock: Nie Huaisang had actually survived that meat grinder, and the man still had the breath to complain. Nobody had the energy to answer him, but Nie Huaisang was already on the verge of weeping happy tears: "Thank the heavens! They're dead, they're finally dead! Survived the impossible... the ancestors truly protected us!"

Riding his relief, a few juniors let out tired cheers, the sound spreading through the cavern.

Amidst the celebration, an anxious cry broke out from the Gusu Lan ranks: "Old Master Lan!"

Lan Qiren’s voice wheezed back instantly: "Hands off me!"

Lan Wangji’s head snapped toward the sound. Lan Qiren was coughing up mouthfuls of dark blood, waving his disciples away as he crossed his legs to steady his breath.

Lan Wangji crossed the room in two strides, taking his uncle's pulse. Right as he channeled spiritual power, Lan Qiren barked, "Stop! Your core hasn't recovered; pouring power into me is like throwing mud into the sea—utterly useless."

Lan Wangji lowered his hands, rising to his feet. Several guest elders turned to him out of sheer habit: "Hanguang-jun, what should we do now?"

The second they asked, they realized the slip. But Lan Qiren kept his eyes shut, showing no sign of reprimand.

Lan Wangji ordered calmly, "Rest for a moment. Tally the casualties. Tend to the wounded without delay."

His authority in Gusu Lan had always been absolute. The disciples took it like a soothing draught, answering in crisp unison: "Yes, sir!"

Before anyone could move a muscle, Wei Wuxian’s voice sliced through the air: "Quiet."

His face was grim as death. The cheers died in people's throats. The entire cavern froze, hundreds of anxious eyes locking onto him. Aside from the sound of ragged, shallow breathing, the hall went dead silent.

And in that suffocating silence, another sound crept in.

It came from outside the cavern—the heavy crunch of dried leaves and snapping twigs.

Not a single set of footsteps. A relentless, endless march.

Nobody dared draw breath. Terrified stares bored into the dark timber outside. Shifting shadows moved through the trees—a massive, black sea creeping forward, vague and shapeless at first, until dragging boots brought them into the moonlight. Ashen complexions, withered talons, and jagged, yellowed fangs.

A fresh horde.

And it was massive—far larger than the first!

The fleeting sliver of hope that had just bloomed in the cavern was crushed to dust, replaced by an abyss of pure, suffocating despair. Even Jin Ling and Lan Sizhui felt cold dread paralyze their limbs. Some cultivators passed out from the shock, while others broke down into soundless, weeping hysterics. Not a single person had the strength left to lift a sword.

Wen Ning had planted himself at the mouth of the cave again, but how long could one man hold back an ocean?

Suddenly, Wei Wuxian called out: "Hanguang-jun!"

Lan Wangji turned. Wei Wuxian took a deep, ragged breath. "I'm going to do something."

The room turned to look.

Wei Wuxian asked, "Will you stand with me?"

Lan Wangji’s pale gaze locked onto his, unblinking and absolute. "Always."

Wei Wuxian flashed a brilliant, blinding grin, and stripped off his black outer robe.

Beneath it was a plain white layer, already stained with red. Dipping his bare fingers into the fresh blood pooling on his hand, he began rapidly painting thick, deliberate runes across his own chest.

As the pattern took shape, the eyes watching him grew wide with horrified disbelief, as if staring at a madman. Fang Mengchen shot to his feet, stammering, "What the hell are you doing?!"

Wei Wuxian ignored him, head down, fingers flying.

When he finally pulled his hand away, the white fabric was no longer a robe. It was a banner.

A Spirit-Attraction Flag—designed to draw every foul, malevolent horror within miles straight to a single living target!

Wei Wuxian stepped up beside Lan Wangji, waving the juniors over. The kids scrambled forward. Jin Ling tried to scramble up too, but Jiang Cheng clamped an iron hand around his shoulder, shoving him down.

"When the second wave breaches, I'm luring them down into the Blood Pool, and Hanguang-jun will handle the kills," Wei Wuxian laid out smoothly. He tapped his chest. "With this target painted on me, they won't spare you a glance. Don't try to be heroes—just run for the exit."

Lan Sizhui’s voice cracked, uncharacteristically loud: "No! Absolutely not!"

Sect Leader Ouyang had given up on restraining his son. Ouyang Zizhen yelled, "Senior Wei, we can still fight! I've got another hundred in me!"

Lan Jingyi was already yanking his belt off. "Paint one on me too! I'll be a flag!"

Wei Wuxian didn't know whether to laugh or cry, grabbing the boy's collar to stop him. "Knock it off, all of you! One target is plenty. Hanguang-jun and I have it covered; the rest of you would just be in the way."

The cavern fell dead silent. Nobody knew how to process what was happening.

Everyone knew what a Spirit-Attraction Flag did. But even if someone were insane enough to use their own living flesh to draw a catastrophic horde just to buy everyone else an escape route... that person was never supposed to be Wei Wuxian!

Lan Sizhui opened his mouth to argue, but Lan Wangji cut in: "Listen to him."

Turning to Lan Qiren, Lan Wangji dropped into a deep, respectful bow. Lan Qiren opened his eyes, silent as stone.

Lan Sizhui pleaded, "Old Master Lan! Hanguang-jun... he... he's..."

Lan Qiren replied softly, "This is what must be done."

Sizhui choked back a sob, "B-But...!!"

Wei Wuxian roared, "Wen Ning! Clear a path!"

The black veins along Wen Ning’s neck surged with violent malice, spider-webbing across his face. Abandoning his defensive stance, he let loose a deafening roar and charged headlong into the fray, tearing a bloody corridor straight through the sea of the dead.

And with the barrier gone, the second horde poured over the threshold of the Demon-Subduing Cave.

Wei Wuxian shoved Lan Sizhui toward the gap. "Go!"
